rmt-2004-geo-01.title: Triangle
rmt-2004-geo-01.body:
Let $O$ be the center of the outer circle. The inner circle is internally tangent to the outer one, so its center is 1 from $O$ and its rightmost point (where the vertical edge of the shaded region touches it) is at distance $1$ from $O$ as well ($-1+2=1$). The vertical edge is a chord of the outer circle at distance 1 from $O$: half-length $y=\sqrt{3^2-1^2}=2\sqrt2$. The shaded region is the triangle with this chord as base ($2y=4\sqrt2$) and apex at the rightmost point of the outer circle, height $3-1=2$. Area $\frac12\cdot4\sqrt2\cdot2=4\sqrt2$.

**Answer: $4\sqrt2$**

rmt-2004-geo-06.title: Geometric series
rmt-2004-geo-06.body:
The first shaded area is $\pi-2$ (circle minus square of side $\sqrt2$). The circle inscribed in that square has half the area of the first circle, so each successive shaded region has half the area of the previous one. Total: $(\pi-2)\left(1+\frac12+\frac14+\cdots\right)=2(\pi-2)=2\pi-4$.

**Answer: $2\pi-4$**
